newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-INTERVIEW - Ashanti year profit falls.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-INTERVIEW - Ashanti year profit falls.

text.p: Ashanti Goldfields Co Ltd's profit for the year to September 30 was below the same period a year earlier but it expects significantly higher profits in future years, a senior company official said on Monday.

"The 12 months ending September 30th, 1996 will be down profits-wise on previous 12 months, but we believe from this level profits will increase significantly," Ashanti chief financial officer Mark Keatley told Reuters an interview.
Ashanti's pre-tax profit for the year to September 30, 1995 slipped 5.5 percent to US$106.2 million.
Ashanti will report the September figure as an interim result as it is moving to a calendar financial year this year.

An anticipated rise in operating costs at the Ghana-based miner's main mine, Obuasi, during fiscal 1995/96 to around US$250 an ounce from US$208 an ounce was the main reason for the fall in full year profits, Keatley said.

Keatley, in Australia to observe the final stage of the merger between Ashanti and Australian-based Golden Shamrock Mines Ltd, based his upbeat outlook on projected improvements in operating costs at Obuasi over the next three years as well as growth in new projects.
The hike in costs at Obuasi was attributed to higher cost sulphide mining operations involving higher stripping ratios, more explosives and higher treatment costs.
Keatley said costs at the mine would come back to between US$220 and US$230 an ounce within three years as it moved from surface mining to a predominantly underground operation.
Underground grades at Obuasi were more than eight grams of gold per tonne compared with about four grams per tonne at surface, he said.
"Over the next three years the contribution the underground operation will roughly double and that we believe will be accompanied by a fall in our average operating costs," he said.

Ashanti's total gold output in the year to September 30 had risen and was expected to hit 1.05 million ounces for the 15 months to December 31 at an average operating cost of US$230 an ounce, Keatley said. Ashanti's production was 932,323 ounces for the year to September 30, 1995.
Mine output would mainly be boosted by the acquisition of gold mines as part of its 80 million stg takeover of Cluff Resources, Keatley said.

Keatley said Ashanti's only debt funding requirements to the end of calendar 1996 were bank-backed project finance for expansion of the Bibiani mine in southwest Ghana and development of the Siguri gold project in Guinea.
"We believe that the financial resources we have on hand are adequate for our next pahse of development ... We have no desire to issue further debt or equity at the corporate level," he said.

Finance for the Bibiani mine would amount to US$50 million while finance needs for Siguri, of which it will hold 70 percent following Australian court approval of the merger with GSM, were yet to be set, Keatley said.
He said he expected the project finance for both projects to be secured in the first half of calendar 1997 at an interest rate slightly above LIBOR plus 105 basis points.
